links.$comment: Only links that resolve today. Leave a value as null and it is omitted from every rendered surface — no dead links, no placeholder buttons.

snapshot.$comment: The system readout. Four rows, not five: anything the masthead already says does not get repeated here. Keep every value under 32 characters — the panel is rendered type, not a reflowing table, and a long value clips instead of wrapping. The build warns if one overflows.

philosophy.$comment: Each line is a lesson from a specific shipped project, with the project named as evidence. If a line cannot be traced to real work, it does not go here.

principles.claim: A negative result gets verified before it gets trusted.
principles.detail: A saturated DNS resolver looks exactly like a dead domain. That bug once put seven working businesses at the top of a call list, so every negative finding is now re-checked in isolation.

principles.claim: Long jobs are resumable or they are not finished.
principles.detail: Discovery covers a market in tiles, centre-outwards, so a run can be stopped, resumed, or split and retried without losing the work already done.

principles.claim: Hand the client the keys, not a support contract.
principles.detail: An embedded Sanity Studio means they publish properties and photos themselves — no code, no second login, no waiting on me.

principles.claim: Every dependency is a future maintenance bill.
principles.detail: A one-page site for a local gym got hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No bundler, nothing to go stale, nothing to migrate in two years.

principles.claim: AI drafts. I decide what ships.
principles.detail: The resolver bug that poisoned a call list was not caught by a model. Scaffolding, tests and review passes come back fast; accountability for whether the thing is correct does not come back at all.
